meaning: subject marker が · marks who/what exists or is asked about
gist: が marks the subject when it is new information or a question word: だれがいますか / [何|なに]がありますか. Question words take が — not ×だれは. Builds on topic は from Unit 1; existence forms います / あります appear here with が.

rows: だれ + が + いますか
[何|なに] + が + ありますか
N + が + います / あります
[猫|ねこ]がいます。 / [本|ほん]があります。
Place + に + N + が + います
[部屋|へや]に[猫|ねこ]がいます。
formation.note: Question words (だれ / 何 / どこ…) take が in existence questions — never ×だれはいますか. が often marks a new or focused subject; は frames a known topic. Place + に pairs with this pattern for located existence.

explanation: が points to the subject of the sentence — often something new, or the answer to who/what. The core classroom questions are だれがいますか (Who is there?) and 何がありますか (What is there?). Do not put topic は on those question words: ×だれはいますか. When you introduce something new in a place, が is natural: 部屋に猫がいます (There's a cat in the room — the cat is new information). When the thing is already known and you say where it is, は is natural: 猫は部屋にいます (As for the cat, it's in the room). Keep that contrast modest: both particles appear with existence; the choice tracks new vs known framing, not a total ban on either pattern.

senses.label: Question words take が
senses.body: だれ / 何 ask with が: だれがいますか / 何がありますか. Never ×だれは… for these.

senses.label: New subject of existence
senses.body: が marks the person, animal, or thing that exists when you are presenting it as new information.
senses.example_en: There is a cat. / A cat is here.

senses.label: Place + が (new info)
senses.body: Placeに + subjectが + います/あります presents what is in that place.
senses.example_ruby: [部屋|へや]に[猫|ねこ]がいます。
senses.example_en: There is a cat in the room.

senses.label: What is there?
senses.body: 何がありますか asks what (thing) exists; answer with Nがあります.

register_context: Classroom default stays polite: います / あります / ですか. Same です/だ habits as Unit 1 when you equate (これは本です). Existence questions with が are the focus here.

mistakes.why: Question words take が in existence questions. ×だれは is ungrammatical here.
何 also takes が when asking what exists — not topic は.
が comes after the subject noun, not before it.

mistakes.wrong_ruby: (Meaning: introducing a cat in the room as new info) [猫|ねこ]は[部屋|へや]にいます。
mistakes.right_ruby: [部屋|へや]に[猫|ねこ]がいます。
mistakes.why: For new information "there's a cat in the room," が on 猫 is the natural pattern. 猫は… fits when the cat is already the known topic.

contrasts.label: が (new) vs は (known topic)
contrasts.summary: 部屋に猫がいます presents the cat as new. 猫は部屋にいます frames a known cat and says where it is.
contrasts.ex_a_ruby: [部屋|へや]に[猫|ねこ]がいます。
contrasts.ex_a_en: There's a cat in the room. (cat = new info)
contrasts.ex_b_ruby: [猫|ねこ]は[部屋|へや]にいます。
contrasts.ex_b_en: As for the cat, it's in the room. (cat = known topic)

contrasts.label: が + います / あります
contrasts.summary: が marks the subject; います / あります say that subject exists. Question words still take が.
contrasts.ex_b_en: Tanaka-san is here. / There is Tanaka-san.

contrasts.label: だれが vs known person は
contrasts.summary: Ask with だれが. Answer or talk about a known person with nameは… when framing that person as the topic.
contrasts.ex_b_ruby: [山田|やまだ]さんは[教室|きょうしつ]にいます。
contrasts.ex_b_en: As for Yamada-san, (he/she) is in the classroom.

examples.ruby: [部屋|へや]に[猫|ねこ]がいます。
examples.english: There is a cat in the room.

examples.ruby: [猫|ねこ]は[部屋|へや]にいます。
examples.english: As for the cat, it is in the room.

examples.ruby: [田中|たなか]さんがいますか。
[図書館|としょかん]に[何|なに]がありますか。
examples.english: What is there in the library?

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.ruby: [部屋|へや]にだれがいますか。

checks.why: Question word だれ takes が: だれがいますか. ×だれは is wrong here.
何がありますか — question words take が.

checks.prompt: Context: introducing a cat in the room as new information.
checks.why: New info in a place → Placeに + Nが + います.

checks.prompt: Context: the cat is already known; you say where it is.
checks.why: Known topic → 猫は…にいます.
